literature_notes: The single ledger line (L1) describes Pcdh-γC4-mCherry, a C-terminal fluorescent-protein fusion. By standard naming convention (ProteinName-Tag), mCherry is appended after the last residue (K938), which lies in the intracellular domain (residues 714–938). The construct was used to validate a PCDHGC4-specific antibody by immunofluorescence in HEK293 cells, confirming that the full-length protein traffics to the cell surface, but the mCherry tag itself is cytoplasmic and does not constitute an extracellular tag insertion. The paper also mentions cMyc-Pcdh-γC5 (N-terminal tag on a different protein) and Pcdh-γC5-EGFP / Pcdh-γC3-EGFP (C-terminal tags on different proteins); none of these are insertions in PCDHGC4. No ledger line reports a tag on the extracellular face of PCDHGC4, so zero sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal mCherry fusion (Pcdh-γC4-mCherry) appended after the last residue K938, which is in the intracellular domain (714–938); used to validate a PCDHGC4 antibody, not an extracellular tag.
